newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-BAYERN WILL NOT CRACK, SAYS STRUNZ.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BAYERN WILL NOT CRACK, SAYS STRUNZ.

text.p: Bayern Munich will not lose their nerve in the German championship race despite seeing their dream of a league and cup double disappear in Karlsruhe on Wednesday, midfielder Thomas Strunz said.

Bayern's expensive array of internationals were eliminated from the cup quarter-finals in a lacklustre 1-0 defeat. But asked if the harmony would now disappear at a club notorious for internal bickering, Euro 96 hero Strunz replied: "I don't think so. There is no reason at all for trouble. It is a cliche but it's true -- the cup has its own rules and it is possible to lose in Karlsruhe."
Bayern travel to seventh-placed Bochum, one of the most improved teams of the season, in the Bundesliga on Saturday and need to forget Wednesday's defeat in a hurry.
The UEFA Cup holders, whose European hopes this season ended with an early-round defeat, looked short of ideas in midfield and shaky at the back.

As one seasoned German football expert observed: "There has been all this talk about whether libero Lothar Matthaeus should play in front or behind the defence. But you have to find the defence first."

Despite their position at the top of the table, Bayern's main problem seems to be consistency. They began the second half of the season last weekend with a convincing victory over St Pauli. Wednesday's defeat was a setback.
"It is disappointing," said captain Matthaeus. "We just did not live up to expectations."
Bayern have a two-point lead over reigning champions Borussia Dortmund who have a superb chance to take the initiative on Friday when they travel to relegation-threatened Fortuna Duesseldorf.

Fourth-placed VfB Stuttgart, the most entertaining team of the first half of the season, need to bounce back from their defeat at Schalke last weekend when they play hosts to Karlsruhe who are fifth, just two points behind.

Both teams are in the semifinals of the German Cup and therefore in the running for a possible double. Wednesday night's draw by national team coach Berti Vogts pitched Stuttgart against Hamburg while Karlsruhe meet minnows Energie Cottbus in the ties on April 15 and 16.
Third-placed Bayer Leverkusen, rated by many as championship material, host mid-table Duisburg on Saturday.
